doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Woody Herman's First Herd and Dave Tough's drumming
summary: He was in the 1944-46 Herman band with Tough, Phillips, Harris and Chubby Jackson, and describes Tough letting the band swing versus Buddy Rich controlling it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Now you were part of which herd?
Well it depends on when you count. Because Woody had some very good bands, a “Band That Played the Blues,” I don’t think they counted from there. I think they counted from
the band that I was on, 1944 to ‘46 with Dave Tough and Flip Phillips and Bill Harris and people like that.
Was Chubby Jackson on that particular band?

Yeah. Well there was, it was the first white band I think that got into what black bands were doing. Not all of them were doing it, but drummers like Jo Jones, Dave Tough was playing more along those lines. The best way I can describe it is prior to that time the majority of drummers were trying to make it happen, just almost like putting in a ring through your nose you know and forcing everybody to play the time you know. And there is something to be said for that and they can get into a good swinging thing, but Dave let the band play, let it happen. He was kind of like a captain that let everybody run the ship but they knew he was the one that would be in control if things went a little awry. I don’t know whether that description —.

Where a great player, there are only a few players that play that way now, that was one of the reasons when Dave would go on a bat, that they had difficulty getting somebody to take his place. Initially many of the people didn’t care for Dave’s playing because they weren’t used to it you know. But once they got used to it, because everybody contributed to the swinging feel this way, rather than — Buddy Rich was a good example. Buddy always controlled the band, although Buddy could play both ways. Because he subbed for Dave one time on a record date and very few people know it and he played just like Dave. But with his ego and his capabilities, you had to make sure that the band knew that he was the one that was driving the coach you know.
